# v1.3.0-479: Windows recognised by what they show, not just their title

Builds on `v1.2.0-474`. A window's title is the weakest way to tell it
apart from its neighbours, and IDEs change theirs every time you open a
file. WLM now also looks at what the window has open and which virtual
desktop it was on.

## Recognising windows

- Visual Studio, Rider, VS Code and Unreal Editor windows are matched by
  the solution, folder or project they have open. A Load finds your
  Visual Studio window for `AlphaApp.sln` whatever file it shows now,
  and two copies of Visual Studio no longer swap places.
- Floating IDE panels (Visual Studio's Error List, Rider's Problems, an
  Unreal tab you dragged out) are told apart by the panel they hold,
  even when every one of them has the same title.
- Each window remembers its virtual desktop. Two Chrome windows on the
  same page, one per desktop, go back to their own desktops' spots.
- Chrome app windows and installed web apps are kept apart from ordinary
  browser windows by their app ID.
- Visual Studio's floating panels are recognised across restarts. Its
  window class changes every time it starts, and that used to lose them.

## Your say over it

- The window editor has a row for each of these: document, panel, app
  ID and desktop. Each shows what was captured and lets you pick
  Default, Require, Prefer or Ignore. Require means "only this exact
  one", Prefer means "use it to choose between lookalikes", and Ignore
  turns it off.
- Load details says what recognised each window, for example
  "recognised by document + panel", and says which required signal kept
  a window from being found.

## Good to know

- Existing profiles load exactly as before. Save or Update a profile
  once to record the new details.
- A capture with Visual Studio open takes a little longer, around half
  a second, while WLM asks Visual Studio which solution it has open.
- Chrome tab addresses and windows pinned to every desktop aren't used
  yet.
